cases.prompt: The requirements in docs/requirements/clinic-booking.md are signed off. How should we organize the work to build this? Give me the plan in chat, don't write files.
rubric: Plan items or slices reference the requirement IDs (FR-x, NFR-x, AC-x) they deliver, so every major item traces to the packet.
It does not plan work for the out-of-scope items (Dentrix integration, payments) beyond noting them as excluded.
It does not present calendar dates or durations as commitments; any timing is relative sequencing or explicitly labelled as an estimate or forecast.
Each named risk has a mitigation or monitoring action, and the undecided SMS provider is treated as a dependency or early decision that affects sequencing.
Testing or verification against the acceptance criteria happens inside the delivery slices, not only as a final phase.
Ownership is stated at least by role, consistent with the stated team (2 developers, part-time designer, client product owner).
Open question Q-1 (clinic opening hours) is carried forward as an open decision rather than silently resolved.

cases.prompt: Make me a delivery plan with sprints and dates for a gym class booking app. We start Monday.
rubric: It points out that there are no validated requirements (scope, users, constraints, team, acceptance criteria) and that the plan therefore rests on assumptions.
Any assumed scope, team size or durations are explicitly labelled as assumptions to confirm.
It asks or lists the specific missing inputs that would change the plan most (for example team size, platform, payments, deadline).
Any dates or sprint lengths are presented as a forecast, not a commitment.

cases.prompt: We have product docs under docs/. Can you put together a phased roadmap from them? Reply in chat.
rubric: Roadmap items cite the source doc each comes from (for example docs/specs/telematics.md).
It sequences telematics ingestion before or with the dispatch board because the board depends on van positions.
It flags the proof-of-delivery spec as a draft with an undecided offline-sync approach, and treats it as a readiness gap or decision point rather than ready work.
It flags the pending vendor webhook docs as a dependency or risk.
It flags the customer tracking link as a goal without a spec, and does not invent its detailed scope.

cases.prompt: krt-compound-master needs a roadmap for the Fleetly initiative from the docs in this repo. Write it as the roadmap artifact.
rubric: Exactly one primary artifact was written (a roadmap, not also a readiness report).
The roadmap has a source inventory and each item names its source doc.
Telematics ingestion is a hard dependency of the dispatch board.
The proof-of-delivery offline-sync decision and the pending vendor webhook docs appear as blockers, user decisions or risks.
